thread.title: Weekly Market Preview: Six Stocks To Watch For the Coming Week (GE, AAPL, BIDU, FB, SBUX, BABA)

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Weekly Market Preview: Six Stocks To Watch For the Coming Week (GE, AAPL, BIDU, FB, SBUX, BABA)
text:
Shutterstock photo Equities closed lower on Friday as the market tried to digest the mixed earnings results received so far from tech bellwethers Amazon ( AMZN ) and Google parent Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ). On Thursday, although its Q2 profits surpassed Street forecasts, Amazon’s revenue wasn’t as robust as investors would liked. And that’s even with its cash cow AWS cloud platform surging 49% year over year.
Amazon, however, is a casualty of a larger concerns among investors as some $5 trillion in value has been erased from global stock and bond markets in October alone. The downward spiral we have witnessed this month has been due to the direction of interest rates, which now puts equities on the verge of entering bear market territory.
According to some analysts, equities continue to be punished due to a combination of higher interest rates and accelerating bond yields. If this selloff continues next week, the Federal Reserve — having hiked rates three times already this year — may be forced to rethink their hawkish stance with regards to interest rates. In the meantime, the recent selloff presents a solid buying opportunity for stocks that are due to report earnings this coming week. Here are a few names to keep on your radar.
General Electric ( GE ) - Reports before the open, Tuesday, Oct. 30
Wall Street expects GE to earn 20 cents per share on revenue of $29.92 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to 29 cents per share on revenue of $33.47 billion.
What to Watch: Trade worries have punished industrial stocks, sending the iShares U.S. Industrials ETF ( IYJ ) down 6% year to date and 8% in three months. And among them, GE has been one of the biggest decliners, losing some 35% of the its value in 2018. With the company ushering yet another CEO change , investors are looking towards 2019. In the near term, however, new CEO Lawrence Culp must convince investors that GE — which has divested a handful of business assets in the last three years — is heading in the right direction. Barclay’s analyst Julian Mitchell upgraded the stock to “Overweight” with a price target of $16, suggesting upside of about 33%.
Facebook ( FB ) - Reports after the close, Tuesday, Oct. 30
Wall Street expects Facebook to earn $1.47 per share on revenue of $13.78 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to $1.59 per share on revenue of $10.33 billion.
What to Watch: Despite the revenue and guidance miss in Q2, Wall Street analysts remain broadly positive about the underlying health of the company, given that some 10% of ad spending in the U.S. this year is expected to go to Facebook. While there continues to be headline risk associated with user privacy and increased risks of U.S. government regulations, Facebook stock, which trades near 52-week lows, remains appealing. On Tuesday Wall Street will want some confirmation that this recent share price correction, driven by tech selloff, is an overreaction.
Baidu ( BIDU ) - Reports after the close, Tuesday, Oct. 30
Wall Street expects Baidu to earn $2.42 per share on revenue of $4.01 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to $3.74 per share on revenue of $3.38 billion.
What to Watch: To what extent has the company’s increased investments in its core search business and artificial intelligence (AI) technologies can continue to pay off? As with most tech stocks, BIDU shares have gotten punished over the past several weeks and trade near 52-week lows. But its efforts to strengthen its mobile search engine and AI technologies are likely to drive top-line growth on Tuesday, while earnings should be boosted by recent divestments of non-core businesses. Combined with efforts to scale up Baidu Cloud with enhanced performance, scalability, storage and edge computing capabilities, the company has tons of growth levers to push the share price higher.
Apple ( AAPL ) - Reports after the close, Thursday, Nov. 1
Wall Street expects Apple to earn $2.78 per share on revenue of $61.59 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to $2.07 per share on revenue of $52.58 billion.
What to Watch: Can Apple shares really reach $310? According to Wedbush Securities analyst Daniel Ives, that answer is yes. The analysts shocked investors last week by giving Apple the the highest price estimate on the Street. Whether he’s right or wrong, we won’t know for some time. The shares are currently trading about 30% below that target. And how quickly they reach that target depends on how many iPhones, particularly the more expensive iPhone X models, Apple sold during the quarter. Ives' believes that about 350 million iPhones could be upgraded in the next 12-18 months. Apple’s guidance on Thursday will offer a clue on both of Ives’s targets.
Starbucks ( SBUX ) - Reports after the close, Thursday, Nov. 1
Wall Street expects Starbucks to earn 60 cents per share on revenue of $6.28 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to 55 cents per share on revenue of $5.7 billion.
What to Watch: The company is expected to report a better-than 3% rise in global same-store sales. While a 3% gain would mark a solid quarter globally, all eyes will be on how Starbucks performed in the U.S. — its largest market. In recent quarters, the U.S. market has been weak, to which analysts have attributed to market saturation. It’s for this reason the company has invested significantly to expand overseas. But to the extent the premium coffee chain can demonstrate strong growth in its bread-and-butter market, Starbucks stock — which has been a stellar performer over the past three months — could be the jolt investors are hoping for.
Alibaba ( BABA ) - Reports before the open, Friday, Nov. 2
Wall Street expects Alibaba to earn $1.06 per share on revenue of $12.47 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to $1.23 per share on revenue of $7.94 billion.
What to Watch: The Chinese e-commerce and tech giant has rolled out various cloud products aimed at meeting the needs of customers who are migrating more towards the realm of Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Internet of Things. For now, the cloud is a relatively small revenue driver for the company, but the management remains confident about the long-term trends of the business. Friday’s results, and the company’s guidance, will reveal how much confidence the management really has and how much investors should put into Alibaba, which has seen its share price tumble 25% in three months.
